articles.title: Viral Video Shows UP Police Dragging Women by Hair During Raid — Inspector Accused of Assault
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking video from Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, has gone viral showing police personnel dragging women by their hair during a raid in the Daranagar Ganj area under Kotwali city limits. According to reports, police had gone to arrest Shivam Kashyap after a dispute with a man named Pramod.

body.html:
A shocking video from Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, has gone viral showing police personnel dragging women by their hair during a raid in the Daranagar Ganj area under Kotwali city limits.

According to reports, police had gone to arrest Shivam Kashyap after a dispute with a man named Pramod. When he wasn’t found, Inspector Sanjay Tyagi allegedly misbehaved with Shivam’s family, pulling his mother’s hair and dragging her along the road. Other women were also reportedly assaulted.

Locals allege that the raid took place on Diwali night, and that the police acted brutally in the name of “swift action.” The incident has sparked outrage on social media, with many calling it an insult to the state government’s “Mission Shakti”, which aims to protect women.

Police officials have stated that an investigation is underway, though no official action has been taken yet against the accused officer.

body.html:
In Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh, police arrested three robbers — Satyam, Satendra Parihar, and Sanjay Verma — for snatching a woman’s mangalsutra near Gopalganj, Orai.

According to the complaint by Maheshwari Devi, she was on her way to buy milk on October 21 around 8 p.m. when three men sneaked up from behind and snatched her mangalsutra before fleeing.

Acting swiftly, police formed special teams and, with the help of CCTV footage and surveillance, arrested all three accused within 12 hours and recovered the stolen jewelry.

The accused, who limped out of the police station after questioning, have been sent to jail.

articles.title: Business Tycoon’s Son Mows Down 6 People, FIR Initially Filed Against ‘Unknown Driver’
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A speeding Jaguar car (UP70 DQ 0070) ploughed through a busy Diwali market in Prayagraj, killing one person and injuring five others, including a child.

body.html:
A speeding Jaguar car (UP70 DQ 0070) ploughed through a busy Diwali market in Prayagraj, killing one person and injuring five others, including a child. The driver — later identified as Rachit Madhyan, son of a prominent businessman and son-in-law of a renowned city doctor — was allegedly drunk and driving at over 100 km/h when the tragedy occurred.

Shockingly, despite police rescuing Rachit from the driver’s seat and sending him to the hospital in an ambulance, the initial FIR was filed against an “unknown driver.” Only after 24 hours was Rachit’s name officially added to the case.

Rachit, 30, is the son of Vasudev Madhyan, owner of the iconic Kamdhenu Sweets, and nephew of Inder Madhyan. He is also the son-in-law of Dr. M.K. Madnani, a renowned hospital operator in Prayagraj. Rachit and his wife, dermatologist Dr. Amrita Madnani, are directors in multiple high-value ventures, including KSN Foods LLP and Madhyan Infratech Pvt. Ltd.

According to eyewitnesses, the Jaguar hit two cars, two bikes, and a scooter, before ramming into a Diwali idol shop. The crash left the shop destroyed and several victims lying in pools of blood.

“The car came at lightning speed — everything was over in 2–3 seconds,” said eyewitness Somil, whose shop was hit.

Another witness, Ramanand Agrahari, alleged that Rachit was heavily intoxicated.

“He was drunk and speeding at around 100 km/h,” Ramanand said.

Sources reveal that Rachit had just returned from a cricket match, where his team had lost and he hadn’t been allowed to bat — possibly leaving him agitated.

The Dhoomanganj Police have now seized the vehicle and sent Rachit’s blood sample for alcohol testing. DCP Manish Shandilya confirmed that CCTV footage and car ownership documents are under scrutiny.

The deceased has been identified as Pradeep Patel, an electrician. His postmortem was conducted on Monday.

The incident has sparked public outrage over alleged police leniency towards an influential family, with many questioning the delay in naming Rachit in the FIR despite his immediate presence at the scene.

articles.title: High-Profile Mystery: Ex-Punjab DGP’s Son Found Dead, Murder Case Filed Against Family
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Panchkula — Aqil Akhtar (33), son of former Punjab DGP Mohammad Mustafa and ex-minister Razia Sultana, was found dead under mysterious circumstances at his residence in Mansa Devi Complex on October 16, 2025.

body.html:
Panchkula — Aqil Akhtar (33), son of former Punjab DGP Mohammad Mustafa and ex-minister Razia Sultana, was found dead under mysterious circumstances at his residence in Mansa Devi Complex on October 16, 2025. What initially appeared to be a case of overdose or natural death has now turned into a high-profile murder probe.

Posthumous videos and social media posts by Aqil have surfaced, alleging shocking family conflicts. In his recordings, Aqil accused his father of having an affair with his wife and claimed that his mother and sister conspired against him. He also stated that he feared being falsely implicated or killed. However, in later videos, Aqil retracted his statements, citing mental illness (schizophrenia) and apologizing to his family — before again expressing fear for his life.

Following a complaint by family acquaintance Shamsuddin Chaudhary from Malerkotla, Haryana Police have filed an FIR against Mohammad Mustafa, Razia Sultana, Aqil’s wife, and sister under charges of murder and criminal conspiracy.

A Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by an ACP-rank officer has been constituted. Police have seized Aqil’s mobile phone, message logs, and videos, which are now undergoing forensic verification. The viscera report is awaited to confirm the cause of death.

The case has sent shockwaves across Punjab’s political circles, with widespread public reaction over the alleged involvement of one of the state’s most influential families in a tragic domestic scandal.
